allowedSourceMaterial.overview: From the mean streets of the Belleville district of Paris to the dazzling limelight of New York's most famous concert halls, Edith Piaf's life was a constant battle to sing and survive, to live and love. Raised in her grandmother's brothel, Piaf was discovered in 1935 by nightclub owner Louis Leplee, who persuaded her to sing despite her extreme nervousness. Piaf became one of France's immortal icons, her voice one of the indelible signatures of the 20th century.

facts.title: La Vie en Rose

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: Can an impoverished singer paralyzed by crippling nerves command the spotlight long enough to reshape 20th-century music?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: Raised in a Belleville brothel and hardened by Parisian streets, young Edith Piaf confronts intense stage fright after nightclub owner Louis Leplée discovers her singular voice in 1935.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Heavy, passionate, and measured; an engaged French-language portrait ideal for solitary, focused viewing.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Olivier Dahan stages the rise of an immortal musical icon as a raw, emotionally heavy drama anchored in the sheer grit required to survive and sing.
